questions.q: Which two CIS specializations did this 13-course path actually build real, repeated hands-on depth in?
options: CIS-HR and CIS-ITSM
CIS-ITSM and CIS-Discovery
Only CIS-CSM
CIS-CSM and CIS-HR
questions.explain: CIS-ITSM was built across Courses 1 and 8, and CIS-Discovery across Course 9 — the two specializations with genuine hands-on coverage in this path.

questions.q: Which two CIS specializations does this lesson honestly admit are NOT covered in depth anywhere in this path?
options: CIS-ITSM and CIS-HR
CIS-CSM and CIS-HR
CIS-ITSM and CIS-Discovery
There are no gaps — this path covers every CIS specialization equally
questions.explain: CIS-CSM (Customer Service Management) and CIS-HR (HR Service Delivery) are real, valid specializations, but this path doesn't build real depth in either.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say to avoid choosing a specialization based on perceived salary differences?
options: All CIS specializations pay exactly the same amount everywhere
There's no reliable, verified module-by-module salary data available, and a credential's real value depends on actual competence built through hands-on practice, not the certificate alone
Perceived salary is actually the single best way to choose
Salary data doesn't exist for any IT certification anywhere
questions.explain: The lesson warns that salary comparisons online tend to be anecdotal, regional, or outdated, and that competence — not the certificate — is what actually matters.

questions.q: What is the first question in this lesson's practical method for choosing a specialization?
options: Which module did you spend the most real, hands-on time configuring across Courses 1-13?
Which specialization has the lowest estimated exam cost?
Which specialization does a random online forum rank highest?
Which specialization has the shortest study guide?
questions.explain: The method starts by looking honestly at where real hands-on depth was actually built, not at outside rankings or guesses.

questions.q: According to this lesson, is choosing CIS-CSM or CIS-HR after finishing this path ever a legitimate choice?
options: Yes, but only if the student ignores all module-specific study entirely
Yes, if it reflects outside interest or a specific target employer — but it means starting that module's study mostly from scratch rather than building on hands-on depth from this path
No, because this path secretly does cover CSM and HR in depth
No, it is never legitimate under any circumstances
questions.explain: The lesson treats CSM or HR as a legitimate direction when it reflects real interest or a target role, while being honest that it requires starting module content from closer to the beginning.
